sources.title: A/72/183–S/2017/621: Nawaf Salam candidate CV, pages 50–51
sources.findings: Read Nawaf Salam candidate CV on printed pages 50–51 of UN A/72/183–S/2017/621: Lebanese citizen, Beirut December 15, 1953; history PhD Sorbonne 1979, Lebanese University law Licence/LLB 1984, Harvard LL.M. 1991, Sciences Po Doctorat d’Etat 1992, plus 1979 DEA and 1974 EHESS Diplôme. Do not convert the latter to a confirmed bachelor degree. Beirut Bar practice 1984–1989/1992–2007, Boston 1989–1992; Harvard visiting research not tenure. AUB associate professor 2003–2007 and department chair 2005–2007. UN ambassador from July 2007; Security Council rotating presidencies May 2010/September 2011, not continuous two-year presidency or UN Secretary-General. Electoral commission member and rapporteur 2005–2006, not automatically enacted reform or title copied from secondary Secretary-General wording. Other candidates’ biographies and original diplomas not independently authenticated.

sources.publisher: Institut des Finances Basil Fuleihan — Lebanon
sources.title: Current prime-minister profile, historical judicial/diplomatic service and degrees
sources.findings: Read current Lebanese Institut des Finances profile: prime minister since February 8, 2025, former UN representative 2007–2017, ICJ member from 2018, elected court president 2024 and resignation after designation. Its “for a nine-year term” wording describes scheduled appointment, not nine years actually completed; exact resignation dates from UN Secretary-General supersede ambiguous shorthand. Three major postgraduate degrees corroborated. No unverified ordinal numbering, political-family role or simultaneous current judicial office adopted.

sources.title: S/2025/37: judicial resignation effective 14 January 2025 and exact service dates
sources.findings: Read full two-page UN Secretary-General S/2025/37, dated January 16, 2025: resignation letter dated January 13, effective January 14, vacancy that day. Judicial service began February 6, 2018; elected/appointed court president February 6, 2024; original judicial term due February 5, 2027. Do not confuse letter/publication/effective dates, judge term with presidency term, or ICJ with ICC. Original ICJ press releases inaccessible; no claim of reading those files or individual judicial case records.

sources.title: S/2025/153, paragraph 54: designation on 13 January and cabinet decree on 8 February 2025
sources.findings: Read paragraph 54 of UN Secretary-General S/2025/153 (March 12, 2025 report): January 13 binding consultations/designation, 84 of 128 MPs supporting candidate, February 8 cabinet decree, 24 ministers including five women. Report date is not appointment date. Only relevant paragraphs inspected; do not claim full conflict annex/complete report audit. Reform-and-rescue label and expressed aspirations are not independently verified completed reform or final peace settlement.

sources.title: January 2025 democracy tracker with February cabinet and confidence-vote updates
sources.findings: Read International IDEA January 2025 tracker and February update: Aoun elected January 9, Salam designated January 13, cabinet February 8, confidence February 26 with 95 votes. Report is institutional secondary synthesis with cited journalism. Expected 2026 parliamentary elections are historical expectation, not verified current event; no assertion about whether those elections occurred. Distinguish 84 designation supporters from 95 later confidence votes and 128 total seats.

sources.title: Government receives 95 confidence votes after parliamentary debate, 26 February 2025
sources.findings: Read LBCI February 26, 2025 concise report: two days debating ministerial statement, 95 votes in favour of confidence. Not a direct popular election and not the same procedure as January nomination. Dynamic surrounding news are unrelated and do not change article date. No full parliamentary roll-call, abstention count or complete policy statement claimed.

sources.title: 25 June 2025 announcement of previous-day US$250 million LEAP financing approval
sources.findings: Read relevant full World Bank June 25, 2025 release body: Board approved yesterday, so June 24; US$250 million financing for LEAP and expandable US$1 billion framework. Infrastructure/services/rubble work, PM office strategic guidance, Public Works and Transport implementation, Environment oversight. Approval, framework size, additional future grants/loans and actual disbursement are distinct. No personal payment, already completed reconstruction or independent 2026 implementation audit inferred from original approval. Avoid mistaking article date for Board decision date.

sources.title: Completed meeting with World Bank delegation, 16 November 2026
sources.findings: Read MTV English November 16, 2026 completed World Bank meeting account: Anna Bjerde, Ousmane Dione, Enrique Blanco Armas and ministers meet Salam at Grand Serail; LEAP, GATE, digitalisation, energy and regional links discussed. Call for accelerated projects and studies is advocacy, not established completion. Not the Turkish president personally visiting because a different report mentions Bilal Erdoğan; not new cabinet appointment.

sources.title: Arabic report of 16 November 2026 World Bank meeting and reform statements
sources.findings: Read Elnashra original Arabic November 16, 2026 article to cross-check English: actual World Bank delegation, relevant ministers, LEAP/GATE/digital projects, energy and economic connectivity, promise of continuing financial/economic/administrative reforms and faster project implementation. No numerical disbursement claim made. Government site matching original announcement found in search but timed out on open, so do not claim primary full statement was read.
